_meta.gate: two gated runs; >=99% per-value cross-run agreement AND movement >= 2x disagreements; falsifiers must fire; only validity == 'valid' cases counted; >=2 carriers for hardware-run
_meta.prefreeze: raw/prefreeze/** is calibration and the post-freeze adversarial probe; it contributes to no gated verdict. The adv01 probe is cited only inside `note` fields and for the two OBSERVATION-status db_defects.
_meta.rt_ok: recorded per case in the raw and used for NO verdict (FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL 3b)
runs: g17p_20260830_run03 (grid, same plan as run01, reverse)

DEF-0174-1.consequence_for_an_emitter: an emitter following db.json writes S into bits 0..6, which the hardware reads as register S>>1 with half-select S&1 -- a wrong register AND a wrong half, silently
DEF-0174-1.db_says: srcA_reg = bits 8..14 (byte+1 bits 0..6); srcA_uni = bit 15 (byte+1 bit 7), enum {0: gpr, 1: uniform/hi}
DEF-0174-1.defect: the byte+1 operand field is modelled one bit off
DEF-0174-1.evidence: raw/g17p_20260830_run01,02 arm B/srcmap, 256 values x 2 plans x 2 runs, 100.000% cross-run agreement, 0 model mismatches on the 64 host-known source values per plan
DEF-0174-1.instruction: n3_mov (and its frame_marker / mov_zext16 siblings, which db.json gives the same field layout)
DEF-0174-1.measured: source register = byte+1 bits 1..7 (aliasing period 64); byte+1 bit 0 = SOURCE HALF select (0 = low 16, 1 = high 16); byte+1 bit 7 = source-register bit 6, observationally inert because of the mod-64 aliasing; no uniform file was ever reached through it

DEF-0174-2.defect: modelled as a 'source-class/size sub-form' and a 'companion / second-operand descriptor'
DEF-0174-2.evidence: the complete 256 x 256 cross-product, 65536 encodings, run three times with 100.000% same-plan cross-run agreement
DEF-0174-2.measured: byte+2 is an OP selector (narrow / move / xor / or) with a source-RELEASE bit at 0x08; byte+3 bit 0 is the DESTINATION-HALF select and the other half is preserved. The accept masks are byte+2 & 0xC0 == 0 with byte+2 & 3 == 1 for the move, and byte+3 & 0x1E == 0.

DEF-0174-3.defect: db.json states 'NOT A STANDALONE HARDWARE OPCODE ... a 2-byte low-nibble-0 slot carrying a trailing operand / immediate / SFU-coefficient WORD of the PRECEDING instruction'
DEF-0174-3.measured: the 4-byte sequence `X0 (2S) 00 01`, placed in a program where the preceding instruction is a completed 2-byte mov_imm, WRITES r[S]'s value into r[X]. Verified for S in {0,1,3,5,8,10,14} and X = 2, in both register plans (raw/prefreeze/adv01, post-freeze adversarial probe).
DEF-0174-3.status: OBSERVATION, NOT A CORRECTED MODEL. This experiment did not sweep the low-nibble-0 group and cannot say whether those four bytes are one instruction or a 2-byte op plus its operand word. What is established is only that they have an architectural effect, which 'not a standalone opcode' does not predict. Recommended follow-up experiment.

DEF-0174-4.defect: db.json's reg_move_c0 semantics block says 'AS OF 2026-08-28 NO VALIDATED GPR-TO-GPR MOVE EXISTS ON APPLE9', and that the byte+2 = 0x01 / op_desc = 0x08 form is 'UNIFORM-REGISTER-SOURCED ONLY -- it FAILS to read a GPR written by falu2/falu2i or by device_load' (EXP-0090)
DEF-0174-4.measured: `2b (2S) 01 00` writes r[S]'s value into r2 for S in {0,1,3,5,8,10,14}, where r[S] was written by mov_imm, in both register plans (raw/prefreeze/adv01). The same 2*S operand encoding as n3_mov. Cross-checked against the plans: byte+1 = 0x0e reads r7, which is 83 in plan idx15 and 0 in plan idx7 -- exactly the two plans' r7 states.
DEF-0174-4.status: OBSERVATION. EXP-0090's negative used falu2/falu2i- and device_load-written sources; device_load on G17P is now known to be ASYNCHRONOUS (DEF-0169-1), which is a candidate explanation for at least that half of its negative. Not swept here. Recommended follow-up.

mov_zext16._corroboration.label: hardware-run
mov_zext16._corroboration.note: This is corroboration of an existing verdict, not a new field. mov_zext16 is a SUB-FORM of n3_mov, not a separate opcode: byte+2's low 3 bits select between narrow (0) and move (1).
mov_zext16._corroboration.range: byte+2 & 0x07 == 0 across the 65536-case cross-product, three runs
mov_zext16._corroboration.semantics: EXP-0161's in-place narrow r[dst] = r[dst] & 0xFFFF is reproduced here as the byte+2 & 0x07 == 0 member of the same instruction, and it is confirmed NOT to be a move: `93 0a 00 01` leaves r5 untouched and sets r9 to r9 & 0xFFFF.

n3_mov._instruction.label: hardware-run
n3_mov._instruction.range: the whole 4-byte instruction GENERATED from db.json's declared bit geometry, with zero bytes copied from any compiled shader, and executed on G17P: 1680 generated half-moves and 840 generated 32-bit copies passed a host-computed 16-register prediction with 0 failures, twice
n3_mov._instruction.semantics: n3_mov is a 16-BIT HALF-REGISTER MOVE with independent source-half and destination-half selection, an optional source release, and a two-source logic mode. A full 32-bit GPR-to-GPR copy r[i] = r[j] is TWO of them, in either order: `i3 (2j+1) 01 01` then `i3 (2j+0) 01 00`.

n3_mov.companion.label: hardware-run
n3_mov.companion.note: db.json calls this a 'companion / second-operand descriptor' whose value 0x01 with subform 0x00 is 'the ZERO-EXTEND high-half-zero companion'. That reading is superseded for the MOVE sub-form: 0x01 does not zero anything, it selects the high half as the destination. PARTIAL REFUTATION of this experiment's frozen H4, recorded: H4 said byte+3 >= 2 must not write; measured, 0x20/0x40/0x80 write exactly like 0x00 and 0x08/0x10 write zero. The X/b3hi falsifier caught it.
n3_mov.companion.range: 0..255 dense x byte+2 in {0x01, 0x09} x 2 register plans, PLUS the complete 256 x 256 cross-product run three times
n3_mov.companion.semantics: byte+3 bit 0 selects the DESTINATION HALF (0 = write the destination's low 16 bits, 1 = write its high 16 bits) and THE OTHER HALF IS PRESERVED in both directions. The write happens iff byte+3 & 0x1E == 0; bits 5..7 are don't-care (byte+3 in {0x00,0x20,0x40,...,0xE0} all write the low half and {0x01,0x21,...,0xE1} all write the high half). byte+3 bits 1 and 2 suppress the write; bits 3 and 4 make it write zero.

n3_mov.dst.label: hardware-run
n3_mov.dst.note: CORRECTS EXP-0168, which reported 'a write whose 4-bit destination nibble is 15 is discarded, and the slot reads 0'. That experiment's read-back path used r15 as its device_store index register and emitted mov_imm(15, 0) immediately before EVERY store, including the one whose data_reg was 15, so r15 was zeroed one instruction before it was read and could not read anything else. Here, in the register plan whose index register is r7, r15 both holds its mov_imm seed (121) and is written correctly by dst = 15. The blind slot of each plan is excluded explicitly and is covered by the other plan.
n3_mov.dst.range: 0..15 dense (all 16 values), both register plans, at the move form; additionally exercised as the destination of all 240 generated 32-bit copies, which is what covers dst == 5 (undecidable in A/dstmap because that arm's source IS r5)
n3_mov.dst.semantics: byte0 bits 4..7 = the destination GPR. r0..r15 all confirmed WRITTEN on hardware against a host-computed 16-register prediction.

n3_mov.srcA_reg.label: hardware-run
n3_mov.srcA_reg.note: DB DEFECT DEF-0174-1. db.json declares srcA_reg = bits 0..6 of byte+1 (instruction bits 8..14) and srcA_uni = bit 7. Measured, the register field is byte+1 bits 1..7 and bit 0 is the source-half select -- the modelled field is shifted by one bit, so an emitter following db.json writes the register number into the wrong bits and gets r[S/2] with a half-select it did not intend. Source registers 16..63 read as 0 in this carrier (192 of 192 cases, both plans, both runs); that is a property of a carrier that allocates 16 GPRs, not a property of the field.
n3_mov.srcA_reg.range: byte+1 dense 0..255 (all 256 values) x 2 register plans; covers source registers 0..127 and both source halves, and spans two aliasing bands
n3_mov.srcA_reg.semantics: MEASURED: byte+1 = 2*S + hs. S = byte+1 bits 1..7 is the SOURCE REGISTER and aliases with period 64 (byte+1 = 2k and byte+1 = 128 + 2k select the same register: 256 of 256 pairs identical, both plans, both runs). hs = byte+1 bit 0 selects which 16-bit HALF of the source is read (0 = low, 1 = high).

n3_mov.srcA_uni.label: hardware-run
n3_mov.srcA_uni.note: DB DEFECT DEF-0174-1 (same defect). db.json's enum {0: 'gpr', 1: 'uniform/hi'} is wrong on the 'uniform' reading: no uniform-file value was ever observed through this bit. The 'hi' reading is right but belongs to byte+1 BIT 0, not bit 7. An emitter should emit 0 and put the half-select in bit 0.
n3_mov.srcA_uni.range: both values, at all 128 byte+1 low-bit combinations, in both plans (the dense byte+1 sweep covers this bit exhaustively)
n3_mov.srcA_uni.semantics: byte+1 bit 7 (instruction bit 15) is SOURCE-REGISTER BIT 6, not a uniform-file selector. Because the register file aliases with period 64, setting it selects r[S+64], which reads identically to r[S]: all 128 (byte+1, byte+1+128) pairs produced byte-identical 16-register dumps in both plans and both runs.

n3_mov.subform.label: hardware-run
n3_mov.subform.note: PARTIAL REFUTATION OF THIS EXPERIMENT'S OWN FROZEN MODEL, recorded rather than smoothed: PRE_REGISTRATION.md H3 froze the move mask as (b2 & 0x03) == 1 and (b2 & 0xE0) == 0, i.e. 8 values. The 65536-case cross-product shows bit 5 is FREE, so the mask is (b2 & 0xC0) == 0 and there are 16 move values. The X/b2hi falsifier caught it independently: byte+2 = 0x21 moves, and it was pre-registered as a value that must not. Bits 2 and 4 are don't-care for the move. The generation arms used byte+2 = 0x01, which is inside both the frozen and the corrected mask, so no generated result depends on this correction.
n3_mov.subform.range: 0..255 dense x byte+3 in {0x00, 0x01} x 2 register plans in the gated sweep, PLUS the complete 256 x 256 byte+2 x byte+3 cross-product (65536 encodings) run three times
n3_mov.subform.semantics: byte+2 is an OPERATION selector, not a 'source-class / size sub-form'. MEASURED on the full cross-product: the MOVE is byte+2 & 0x03 == 1 with byte+2 & 0xC0 == 0 -- exactly the 16 values {1,5,9,...,61} reach the destination's HIGH half, and those same 16 plus the 24 two-source-logic values reach the LOW half. byte+2 & 0x07 == 0 is the IN-PLACE NARROW (r[dst] &= 0xFFFF, byte+1 inert), which is the member db.json splits out as mov_zext16 and EXP-0161 validated. byte+2 & 0x07 == 3 behaves as XOR and == 4 as OR of the byte+1 and byte+3 operands. BYTE+2 BIT 3 (0x08) RELEASES THE SOURCE, and the release is HALF-GRANULAR: it zeroes exactly the 16-bit half that was read and leaves the other half intact (post-freeze adversarial probe, raw/prefreeze/adv01).
